recommendation: Keep this source-changing commit. It directly applies the published CBCC request without changing Consent conformance rules; further work is only needed if the work group wants to define intentional multi-consent patient pairings.
issue_request: FHIR-22682 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core Consent after a 2019 CBCC vote. It asked that standalone Consent examples identify different patients so a single patient does not appear to have multiple Consent resources, with only intentional purpose/type exceptions.
initial_application: No local git commit explicitly mentioned FHIR-22682. Consent examples were reworked in ea72f27bd154 and adjusted in bbe7cd28eae near the Jira resolution window, but the current branch still reused Patient/f001, Patient/f002, and Patient/example across multiple standalone Consent example subjects.
additional_context: Consent is an active resource in source/fhir.ini and the Consent examples live under source/consent, with list-Consent-examples.xml identifying the example collection. Quoted Zulip and Confluence searches found no community record that narrows, reverses, or supersedes the Jira request.
reconciliation: Changed the affected Consent example subject references to distinct Patient references and updated matching display or narrative patient names. In consent-example-CDA.xml, also changed the grantee reference because that example says the patient signs for themself.
